# Mireward

Map Key & Accompanying Gazetteer

A practical GM reference for Mireward, the last walled town on the Mireward Reach before the fen-facing north. This file promotes selected scaffold material into reference form for Session 23 scene grounding. It does not retroactively prove anything happened at the table; played facts still come from Session Recaps and session memory.

## Quick Key

| # | Location | Scene Use | Anchor NPC(s) / links |
|---|----------|-----------|-----------------------|
| 1 | Reach Gate / Mud Apron | Session 23 opening threshold; short-handed garrison, wagon pressure, Lysandra homecoming | `Elderwyld/Cities and Towns/Mireward/NPCs/lysandro_ironveil/character_seed.md` |
| 2 | Tithe Barn / Crown Compound | Refugee overflow, grain/requisition fights, muster rolls, armory access | TBD |
| 3 | Ferry Slip / Causeway Head | Fen smell, northbound bottleneck, wagons stopping before wet ground | TBD |
| 4 | The Last Dry Bed | Inn floor, rumor hub, no rooms, Orin/Maera pressure upstairs | Planned dossier |
| 5 | Well / Pump Square | Queues, ration fights, bad-water dread | TBD |
| 6 | Bell / Shrine Square | Patrol widows, public prayer, festival echoes from the south | TBD |
| 7 | Garrison / Reeve Office | Who holds authority when crown, town, and wall needs conflict | TBD |
| 8 | Refugee Camp | Human-scale capacity pressure inside or just outside the wall | TBD |
| 9 | Downwind Craft Lane | Tanners, fullers, lime, charcoal; honest stink-trade identity | TBD |
| 10 | Conical Crown | Optional pre-era skyline set dressing; use only if the scene needs wonder or hazard | TBD |

## Gazetteer

## 1. Reach Gate / Mud Apron

See `Elderwyld/Cities and Towns/Mireward/Mireward_Location_Dossiers/reach_gate_mud_apron.md`.

This is the party's first threshold into Mireward: torchlight on wet wall, mud under wagon wheels, and a competent but thin watch deciding who gets through after tenth bell. The gate should feel functional, not ruined. Mireward's wall still matters. The trouble is that the festival pulled a slice of young spears south, one or more long patrols are still out, and the refugee pressure is arriving faster than the town's habits can absorb.

## 2. Tithe Barn / Crown Compound

The tithe barn is where Mireward's chartered usefulness becomes physical: grain, legal weight, storage, ledgers, and official reluctance. In a normal season it is bureaucracy with sacks. In Session 23 prep it can become the cleanest pressure point for refugee overflow, requisition conflict, and the question of whether the town spends stored food before someone with a seal says yes.

## 3. Ferry Slip / Causeway Head

The ferry slip and causeway head mark the beginning of wet-country logistics. Use this as the place where carts become arguments, fen smell starts to win over road dust, and rumors from north of town arrive in fragments rather than reports.

## 4. The Last Dry Bed

The Last Dry Bed is the reach inn: last hot meal before the smell, full rooms, floor space if someone vouches, and the most human-scale version of Mireward's denial. Its Orin/Maera beat remains a planned dossier until promoted separately.

## 5. Well / Pump Square

The well or pump square is the pressure gauge for the town. If the queue is orderly, Mireward is coping. If the queue fractures, the whole Session 23 opening can feel like a crisis without needing a monster in the street.

## 6. Bell / Shrine Square

The bell and shrine square carry patrol-family memory. This is where widows, kin, and old garrison households can pray for Mirathorn festival safety while the northern edge of the map gets worse.

## 7. Garrison / Reeve Office

Authority is still an open knob: reeve, mayor, sergeant-emeritus council, or joint arrangement. Do not lock the structure until the table needs a speaking office. The important established pressure is that Mireward has real patrol culture and is short-handed by festival pull plus long patrol timing, not because it rotted.

## 8. Refugee Camp

The refugee camp, whether inside the wall, in haylofts, in the tithe barn, or just beyond the palisade, is the visible proof that Mireward's road economy is a lagging indicator. The apron can still look fine while the town's capacity is failing.

## 9. Downwind Craft Lane

Downwind craft lane is the stink-trade quarter: tanners, fullers, lime, charcoal, dye, and other work that wanted distance from Mirathorn guild windows. This is core identity, not comic relief. The smell is part of the town's claim that honest work does not need spires.

## 10. Conical Crown

Optional set dressing only. A conical hill or ponded crown on the skyline can connect the Reach to older pre-era weirdness, but it should not become the town's primary identity unless play pulls it forward.

## GM Use Note

Mireward is not a collapsed frontier ruin. Play it as a working pension-and-road town caught at the wrong moment: competent walls, thin garrison, refugee pressure, festival-deaf south, and a proud not-Mirathorn identity being tested before it has language for the test.

## Reach Gate / Mud Apron

Mireward's first table-facing threshold: wet road, torchlit palisade, a mud apron crowded by wagons and foot traffic, and a watch that is competent enough to hold the line but too thin to make it look easy.

# At a Glance

The gate is not a ruin and not a joke. It is a working Reach gate under strain. The palisade still stands; the wall walk still has people who know how to count heads; the apron still does business. The fracture is timing: festival duty pulled young spears south, a long patrol is still out, and the north is sending frightened people toward the town faster than Mireward's ordinary systems can process them.

# Quick Reference

| Use | Detail |
|-----|--------|
| Opening beat | The party arrives after dark, outside the wall, with wagons and animals in bad weather. |
| Authority feel | Practical gatekeeping: foot traffic can be handled; wagons, axles, and panic wait until dawn unless someone is bleeding or useful. |
| Town signal | The apron still looks profitable and orderly from a distance, but the haylofts and queues tell the real story. |
| Anchor NPC | `Elderwyld/Cities and Towns/Mireward/NPCs/lysandro_ironveil/character_seed.md` — Lysandro Ironveil, gate emeritus and Lysandra's father. |
| Open knob | Who formally runs Mireward remains undecided: reeve / mayor / sergeant-emeritus council / joint authority. |

# Sensory Profile

Cold drizzle on oiled wood. Torch smoke flattening under wet air. Mud sucking at wagon wheels. Old iron hinges. A wall-bell that sounds practical rather than grand. The smell changes when the wind shifts: road animals and wet wool first, then lime, leather, and downwind craftwork from inside the town.

# Physical Description

The gate opens onto a broad mud apron built for trade, tithe checks, ferries, and overnight road traffic. It was never meant to absorb a refugee surge and late-night wagon bottleneck at the same time. A tithe scale or counting post sits close enough to make every argument feel official. The wall walk above is patched, used, and familiar to locals. Its wear reads as maintenance, not neglect.

The apron should give the players three immediate truths: Mireward is real, Mireward is full, and Mireward has not yet admitted to itself that those two facts are in conflict.

# People Here

## Lysandro Ironveil — gate emeritus

Use the existing seed for voice and family continuity. He is the wall's warm, loud, embarrassing competence: anti-authoritarian in speech, reliable in duty, and entirely capable of turning a gate policy argument into a public story about his daughter.

## Green gate kids

The remaining young watch are the ones who drew the unglamorous post while show uniforms and quick spears went south for festival duty. They are not useless. They are visibly aware that they are being watched by veterans, refugees, and now heroes.

## Apron folk

Inn runners, axle hands, drovers, late arrivals, tired animals, and people trying to convert fear into procedure. They are the best place to show the difference between road commerce and refugee crush.

# What This Place Offers

- A hard threshold before the party enters town.
- A natural place to foreground Lysandra's homecoming without forcing a monologue.
- A visible capacity problem: wagons, foot traffic, animals, and families all needing different answers.
- A place to introduce the garrison-thin-by-coincidence premise without saying it as exposition.

# Town News & Rumor

- The festival took some of the young spears south, and people disagree about whether that was patriotic, foolish, or simply normal.
- A long patrol is still out on fen rotation. It is not yet late enough for official panic, which makes private worry worse.
- Some refugees insist the danger is north and wet; others will only say the road behind them is wrong.
- The inns look busy enough for the south to misunderstand the town as prosperous rather than overloaded.

# Hidden Tension

The gate's real conflict is not whether Mireward is defended. It is whether competent locals can keep using ordinary gate logic when the situation has stopped being ordinary. If the party helps, Lysandro and the apron folk notice whether they solve the human problem or only demand entry.

# Source and Authority Notes

- S22 play canon supports only the arrival-at-wall/gate beat and Lysandro identifying Lysandra as his daughter.
- Garrison thinness, festival pull, long patrol timing, refugee pressure, and town identity are promoted scaffold material for Session 23 planning.
- This file is reference/world grounding after promotion; it must not be cited as proof of what happened in Session 22.
